Phase 0 — Setup

  • Pool: 10.0.0.10–10.0.0.89 (80 IPs), lease time 60s
  • 5 local DNS entries: nas / mail / print / ws / fileserver .corp.local → 10.0.0.20–24
  • DNS server set to 10.0.0.100 (served via DHCP offer to all clients)

Phase 1 — DORA Storm: 60 concurrent clients

  • 30 workstations (ws-01–30, CT 300–329) + 15 IoT (iot-01–15, CT 330–344) + 15 mobile (mob-01–15, CT 345–359) — started simultaneously
  • All 61 leases acquired in 5 seconds — 77% pool utilisation (62/80 IPs)
  • Each client received: IP from 10.0.0.10–89, gateway 10.0.0.1, DNS 10.0.0.100

Phase 2 — DNS Storm: ~400 QPS sustained

  • 60 CTs each queried 16 domains/cycle: 6 allowed, 5 blocked (ad trackers), 5 local (corp.local)
  • Sustained ~400 QPS cluster-wide; query log filled to 10,000 entries (ring buffer max)

Phase 3 — Multi-node sysadmin: any of 3 nodes accessible

  • All 3 nodes queried independently — lease data consistent via ForwardWrite leader-proxy

Phase 5 — Raft Failover mid DNS storm

  • Leader skoed-1 (10.0.0.100) stopped while all 60 CTs had active DNS queries running
  • New leader elected: skoed-2 (10.0.0.101) in 6.4 seconds (Raft term 13)
  • DNS traffic resumed on new leader immediately
